name: Forgejo
description: Git hosting with pull requests, issues, a package registry and built-in CI in one small program. It began as a fork of Gitea in 2022 and is now an independent project under a non-profit umbrella. It is the software behind Codeberg.
backing: Developed under the umbrella of Codeberg e.V., a German non-profit, with open community governance

maturity.rationale: Builds on the Gitea codebase dating from 2016 and hosts hundreds of thousands of repositories on Codeberg. Actions and federation are the parts still maturing.

selfHosting.summary: A single binary or container with SQLite, PostgreSQL or MySQL. Running CI adds a separate runner, which deserves some thought about isolation because it executes whatever your repositories tell it to.

requirements.notes: CI runners need their own resources, sized for your builds.

managedHosting.label: Codeberg
managedHosting.note: Free hosting for free and open-source projects, run by the non-profit behind Forgejo

strengths: A tiny footprint: a small VPS hosts a whole team
Built-in migration pulls repositories, issues, pull requests, labels, milestones and releases from GitHub
Forgejo Actions uses a workflow syntax modelled on GitHub Actions, so many workflows move with small edits
Package registry, wiki and project boards with no paid tier
weaknesses: Actions is designed to be familiar rather than identical: workflows that lean on GitHub-hosted runners or marketplace actions need work
No network effect: no stars to chase and few drive-by contributors
Code search and review tooling are simpler than GitHub's or GitLab's
Federation between forges is still in development

featureNotes.ci-cd: Forgejo Actions, with a separately installed runner
featureNotes.actions-compat: Similar syntax; not every action or context works
featureNotes.pages: Through a separate pages server or a CI job
